title: Triage drills: six sets of five tickets
summary: Practise ordering a queue. Each set has five tickets; you assign severity, priority and a next action, then compare with a model answer.

lessons.title: Triage sets 1 to 3
lessons.body:
Triage means deciding, for each new ticket, what it is, how serious, how soon, who next and what to say to the customer. In the drills you place five tickets in order. Use the same scales as the earlier lessons.

**Severity** (impact if it happens): Critical (down, data loss, safety, no workaround), Major (core function broken for many, painful workaround), Moderate (some users or a reasonable workaround), Minor (cosmetic).

**Priority** (order of work): P1 now, P2 this sprint or sooner, P3 next sprint, P4 backlog. The practice tickets.csv file uses low, medium, high and critical for severity. Map them as low = Minor, medium = Moderate, high = Major, critical = Critical.

**Five questions per ticket.**

1. What type is it: incident, bug, access, how-to, feature request, data fix?
2. How many customers, and is there a workaround?
3. Is there a clock: a deadline, an SLA, a shift starting soon?
4. Is it a duplicate of something open?
5. What is the next action and who owns it?

**Worked example.**

```text
T1 'Cannot assign anyone to shifts, all of Riverside's dispatchers' -> Incident, Critical-to-Major, P1: core function, whole customer, shift deadlines. Next: confirm, page on-call, update customer in 15 min.
T2 'Typo on login page' -> Bug, Minor, P4. Next: backlog.
T3 'How do I export monthly assignments' -> How-to, Minor, P4. Next: send article, link ticket to article.
```

Order: T1, T3 (quick answer, closes fast), T2.

A quick win that costs a minute, such as sending an existing article, can go first even at low priority, as long as it does not delay a P1.

Write your answer as a list: ticket, type, severity, priority, next action, order. Mark yourself against the rubric.
keyPoints: Triage answers type, severity, priority, owner and next action for each ticket.
Look for a clock: a shift starting soon or an SLA about to breach.
Check for duplicates and for a workaround before you rank.
Quick wins that do not delay a P1 can go early.
lessons.interviewAngle: A common practical test is 'here are five tickets, what do you do first?'. Think aloud with the five questions, say your assumptions, and give an order with reasons. Showing the reasoning matters more than agreeing with the model order.

exercises.prompt: Which ticket do you handle first? (a) Typo on the login page. (b) No dispatcher at one customer can assign shifts; emergency shifts start in two hours. (c) Request for a new report. (d) How do I export?
exercises.explanation: Core function down for a whole customer with a time-critical clock is the highest severity and priority.

exercises.prompt: Set 1. Triage in order (type, severity, priority, next action): (T1) Alerts for emergency shifts have not been sent to anyone for 40 minutes, several pharmacies calling. (T2) Dispatcher at Pharmacy 9 asks how to repost a cancelled shift. (T3) Request: add a column for licence state to the pharmacist list. (T4) Text on the mobile app login says 'Pasword'. (T5) New dispatcher at Pharmacy 14 cannot log in after reset.
exercises.answer:
Order: T1, T5, T2, T3, T4.
- **T1** Incident, Critical, P1: core alerting down, multiple customers. Page on-call, declare SEV 1 or 2, link all calls, update customers in 15 minutes.
- **T5** Access, Moderate to Major (blocks that user), P2: check account and reset; escalate if the account is active and reset fails. Reply within the hour.
- **T2** How-to, Minor, P4 but quick: send the repost article and close; link the ticket to the article.
- **T3** Feature request, Minor, P4: log, ask for use case, add to backlog.
- **T4** Bug, Minor, P4: log, batch with the next release.
rubric: T1 is first with incident handling
T5 ranked above the how-to because a user is blocked
Quick how-to handled with an article
Feature and typo placed in the backlog
Each has a next action

exercises.prompt: Set 2. (T1) Duplicate assignment created on double click: reported by 3 pharmacies this week; pharmacists get two texts. (T2) Report total does not match the roster for one pharmacy, month-end billing is tomorrow. (T3) Where do I see who accepted a request? (T4) Pharmacy asks for a bulk upload of shift requests. (T5) Pharmacist cancelled shift still shows as assigned on the pharmacy's view.
exercises.answer:
Order: T2, T5, T1, T3, T4.
- **T2** Data fix / bug, Major, P1 or P2 with a deadline tomorrow: investigate the totals today, tell the customer what to expect.
- **T5** Bug, Major, P2: a pharmacy may rely on a pharmacist who cancelled; confirm with data and warn the pharmacy as a workaround.
- **T1** Bug, Moderate, P2 or P3: a known repeating issue; link all three reports to one primary ticket, confirm the workaround of one click.
- **T3** How-to, Minor, P4: article, link ticket.
- **T4** Feature request, Minor, P4: log with volume.
rubric: Deadline on T2 raises its priority
T5 treated as a risk to coverage
T1 linked as one primary ticket
How-to answered with an article
Feature recorded with context

exercises.prompt: Set 3. (T1) A pharmacy manager emails: 'You told me Friday. It is Monday and nothing.' about a time zone bug. (T2) Data fix: 12 assignments from last week need their completed date corrected. (T3) Three new dispatchers at one customer need accounts by tomorrow. (T4) The reports page takes 20 seconds to load. (T5) Security: a former employee of Pharmacy 22 can still log in.
exercises.answer:
Order: T5, T1, T3, T2, T4.
- **T5** Access/security, Critical to Major, P1: disable the account now, check what was accessed, report per policy.
- **T1** Missed promise, Major customer-relationship risk, P2: reply today with an honest status, new date and owner; check the bug's priority.
- **T3** Service request, Moderate, P2 (deadline tomorrow): create accounts today.
- **T2** Data fix, Moderate, P3: needs approval and a backup, schedule.
- **T4** Bug/performance, Minor to Moderate, P3: collect data on which report and when; log.
rubric: Security placed first
Missed promise handled with an update, not a defence
Service request with a deadline ranked above the data fix
Data fix includes backup or approval
Performance ticket asks for specifics

lessons.title: Triage sets 4 to 6
lessons.body:
The second drill adds ambiguity. Real queues are messier than the first set: tickets arrive with missing information, with pressure from a loud customer, or with a link to a bigger problem. The mark is for reasoning, not for guessing the 'right' order.

**Extra checks for harder sets.**

- **Information gap.** If you cannot rate a ticket, your next action is a question, and your priority is provisional. Say 'provisional P3 until I know X'.
- **Loud versus important.** Customer tone is not severity. A calm report of data loss outranks an angry report of a typo. Give the angry customer a prompt, honest reply anyway.
- **Pattern.** Five tickets about the same thing are one problem. In the practice tickets.csv, the title 'Duplicate assignment created on double click' appears 50 times: that is a candidate for a problem record and a root-cause fix, not 50 separate bug fixes.
- **Dependencies.** A ticket may wait on another. Link it and record the dependency.
- **Capacity.** If everything is P1, nothing is. State what you would defer to make room.

**Worked example of a provisional rating.**

```text
T 'Pharmacist assigned to two shifts at the same time' -> Bug/data, Major (double-booking), P2 provisional.
Question: are both shifts real and overlapping? Is it one pharmacist or many?
Action: pull the two assignments by SQL, confirm overlap, warn the dispatcher.
```

When you present your triage, give the order, the reasoning in one line each, and the questions you still have. State your assumptions out loud, as you would in an interview or practical test. Then mark yourself against the rubric.
keyPoints: If a ticket cannot be rated, the next action is a question and the priority is provisional.
Many tickets with one title are one problem, so open a problem record.
If everything is P1, state what you will defer.
lessons.interviewAngle: These sets mirror the 'two urgent tickets at once' interview question. Reason out loud: impact, clock, workaround, then communication. Mention checking the repeated tickets in SQL if the data exists, because that is your real skill. Close with the questions you would ask before committing, which is what a hiring manager is listening for.

exercises.prompt: An angry customer reports a typo; a calm customer reports that cancelled shifts are being counted as filled in billing totals. Which gets the higher severity?
choices: The calm billing-totals report, because it affects money and data accuracy
exercises.explanation: Severity follows impact, not tone. The angry customer still gets a prompt, honest reply.

exercises.prompt: Set 4. (T1) 'Text message when a shift is filled' requested again by a 4th customer. (T2) A pharmacist reports being assigned to two overlapping shifts. (T3) 'Alert was not sent to nearby pharmacists' for one shift at Pharmacy 35. (T4) Customer demands a call-back within the hour about a wrong report total, no details. (T5) How do I add a new pharmacy location?
exercises.answer:
Order: T2, T3, T4, T5, T1.
- **T2** Bug/data, Major, P2 provisional: double-booking risk; confirm overlap with SQL.
- **T3** Bug, Major, P2: check alert log for the shift and look for a pattern with the other alert failures; link.
- **T4** Unknown, provisional P3: call back within the hour to gather details (which report, what total, what expected), since the promise costs little and the details set severity.
- **T5** How-to, P4: send the article and link.
- **T1** Feature request, P3 backlog: attach to the existing request, increase the count and add the 4th customer as evidence.
rubric: Overlap ticket treated as a data risk
Alert ticket linked to a pattern
Information gap handled with a call and a provisional priority
Request merged with the existing one
Reasoned order

exercises.prompt: Set 5. (T1) Fifty tickets in 9 months titled 'Duplicate assignment created on double click'. What do you do with them as a set? Then triage today's new ones: (T2) another duplicate-assignment ticket. (T3) A pharmacist cannot see their schedule on iOS. (T4) Export file has the wrong date format for one customer. (T5) Request for dark mode.
exercises.answer:
**T1 set:** treat as a pattern: open a problem record, link all 50, count affected pharmacies and the cost (duplicate texts, wasted time), and escalate for a root-cause fix (prevent duplicate submit, add a unique constraint) instead of fixing each case. Publish a workaround article.
**Today:** Order: T3, T2, T4, T5.
- **T3** Bug, Major to Moderate, P2: pharmacist cannot see assignments; check version and account, reproduce.
- **T2** Bug, Moderate, P2: link to the problem record and give the workaround, escalate the pattern.
- **T4** Bug, Minor, P3.
- **T5** Feature request, Minor, P4.
rubric: Recognises the repeat pattern and opens a problem record
Recommends root cause not case-by-case fixes
Links the new duplicate to the record
Sensible order for today's tickets

exercises.prompt: Set 6. You are alone on support and all five arrive in 10 minutes. (T1) SMS provider status page shows an outage. (T2) Pharmacy 3 cannot assign shifts. (T3) New dispatcher at Pharmacy 18 needs an account today. (T4) Question about invoice format. (T5) Request: change the alert radius default. Order them, say what you defer and what you tell the people waiting.
exercises.answer:
Order: T1 and T2 together (check whether related), T3, T4, T5.
- **T2** is the highest immediate impact: core function down at a customer. Check if the same cause as **T1**: SMS outage affects alerts, not assignment, so probably separate. Escalate T2 now.
- **T1** Incident, Major, P1: confirm which flows depend on the provider, post an internal note and a customer notice, and use the manual workaround for urgent shifts.
- **T3** Service request, P2: do after the escalations, same day.
- **T4**, **T5** deferred: send a holding reply with the time I will respond (tomorrow morning).
To people waiting: a short message with the exact time I will reply.
rubric: Checks whether tickets share a cause
Highest impact first, then the incident
Explicit deferral of low-priority tickets
Holding replies with times
